This is version v3.4 of the Secure Coding Policy, effective from 2022-07-14 and maintained by the Engineering department.

## Purpose

This policy sets out the practices developers follow so that the software the company builds resists common attacks.

## Scope

It applies to all developers and to all code written for the company or its clients.

## Rules

- All input from users and other systems is validated, and database queries use parameters rather than text built from input.
- Passwords, keys and other secrets are never written into source code; they are kept in the approved secrets store.
- Third-party libraries come from trusted sources, are scanned for known vulnerabilities and are kept up to date.
- Authentication, authorisation and encryption use the company's standard libraries, not home-made implementations.
- Security-relevant code is reviewed by a second developer, and automated security scans run on every build.

## Responsibilities

Developers complete secure coding training every year. Team leads make sure findings from scans and reviews are fixed before release.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Engineering department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.2 of the Code Review Standards, effective from 2025-03-08 and maintained by the Engineering department.

## Purpose

These standards make sure that every change to the company's source code is checked by a second person before it reaches the main branch.

## Scope

They apply to all repositories that hold production code, infrastructure definitions or shared libraries.

## Rules

- Every change is submitted as a pull request and approved by at least one reviewer who did not write it.
- Reviewers check correctness, readability, test coverage, security and the effect on performance, not only coding style.
- Automated builds, tests and static analysis must pass before a pull request can be merged.
- Pull requests should be small enough to review properly; large changes are split into logical parts.
- Review comments are answered or resolved before merging, and urgent fixes merged without review are reviewed afterwards within one working day.

## Responsibilities

Authors explain what a change does and how it was tested. Reviewers respond within one working day. Team leads make sure the standards are followed.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Engineering department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.8 of the Engineering Quality Standards, effective from 2023-08-07 and maintained by the Engineering department.

## Purpose

These standards define the minimum level of quality that software must reach before it is delivered to a client or released to production.

## Scope

They apply to all engineering teams and to all software the company builds or maintains.

## Rules

- New code is covered by automated tests, and the build must pass before a change is merged.
- Every release has acceptance criteria agreed with the product owner and is tested against them.
- Defects are logged, given a severity and fixed within the time agreed for that severity; critical defects block a release.
- Performance, security and accessibility are tested for every major release, not only functional behaviour.
- After a production incident the team holds a blameless review and records the actions that will prevent a repeat.

## Responsibilities

Engineering managers are accountable for quality in their teams. Quality Assurance verifies releases independently and reports on quality trends.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Engineering department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.7 of the Version Control Guidelines, effective from 2023-05-27 and maintained by the Engineering department.

## Purpose

These guidelines describe how source code is stored, branched and released, so that the history of every change is clear.

## Scope

They apply to all source code, configuration and infrastructure definitions maintained by the company.

## Rules

- All code is kept in the company's version control system; nothing is developed only on a personal machine.
- Work is done on short-lived branches that are merged into the main branch through reviewed pull requests.
- Commit messages say what was changed and why, and refer to the related task.
- The main branch is always in a state that can be released, and every release is tagged with a version number.
- Large binary files, generated files and secrets are not committed to a repository.

## Responsibilities

Developers follow the branching rules. Repository owners protect the main branch and keep access to the repository up to date.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Engineering department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.6 of the AI Model Governance Policy, effective from 2025-03-23 and maintained by the Artificial Intelligence department.

## Purpose

This policy sets out how artificial intelligence and machine learning models are approved, released and monitored so that they stay accurate, fair and safe throughout their life.

## Scope

It applies to every model that is built, bought or fine-tuned by the company and used in a product, an internal tool or a business decision.

## Rules

- Every model must have a named owner and an entry in the model register before it is used in production.
- A model may only be released after a documented review of its training data, evaluation results, known limitations and intended use.
- Models that influence decisions about people, money or security are classed as high risk and need sign-off from the AI governance board.
- Production models are monitored for accuracy, drift and bias, and are re-evaluated at least every six months.
- A model that fails its agreed thresholds must be rolled back or switched off until the cause is understood and fixed.

## Responsibilities

Model owners keep the documentation and monitoring up to date. The AI governance board reviews high-risk models and keeps the register.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Artificial Intelligence department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v2.2 of the Machine Learning Development Standards, effective from 2023-02-04 and maintained by the Artificial Intelligence department.

## Purpose

These standards describe how machine learning models are developed so that results can be reproduced, compared and trusted.

## Scope

They apply to all teams that train, evaluate or deploy machine learning models.

## Rules

- Code, data versions, parameters and results of every experiment are tracked, so that any result can be reproduced.
- Training, validation and test data are kept separate, and test data is never used to tune a model.
- A model is compared against a simple baseline and evaluated on the agreed metrics before it is proposed for release.
- Data sets are checked for quality, bias and licence restrictions before they are used for training.
- Models are packaged with a model card that states the intended use, the training data, the evaluation results and the known limitations.

## Responsibilities

Data scientists and machine learning engineers follow these standards in their daily work. Team leads review experiments and model cards before release.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Artificial Intelligence department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v2.1 of the Responsible AI Usage Policy, effective from 2026-02-23 and maintained by the Artificial Intelligence department.

## Purpose

This policy explains how employees may use artificial intelligence tools, including the company's own assistant, safely and responsibly.

## Scope

It applies to all employees and contractors who use AI tools for company work.

## Rules

- Confidential, personal or customer data is entered only into AI tools that the company has approved for that kind of data.
- AI output is checked by a person before it is used in a decision, sent to a client or added to a product.
- AI is not used to make decisions about hiring, pay or discipline without human review.
- Content produced with AI is not presented as solely one's own work where a client or the law requires disclosure.
- Errors, biased results or misuse of an AI tool are reported to the AI governance board.

## Responsibilities

Each user remains responsible for the work they deliver with the help of AI. The AI governance board approves tools and reviews reported problems.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Artificial Intelligence department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.5 of the Data Management Policy, effective from 2022-08-12 and maintained by the Quality Assurance department.

## Purpose

This policy sets out how the Quality Assurance department classifies, stores, shares and retires the data it creates and uses.

## Scope

It applies to all data owned or processed by the Quality Assurance department, whether in databases, documents, spreadsheets or reports.

## Rules

- Every data set has an owner and a classification: public, internal, confidential or restricted.
- Data is stored in the approved systems for its classification, never only on a personal device.
- Confidential and restricted data is shared on a need-to-know basis and with the owner's approval.
- Important data is backed up, and the backups are tested by restoring them at least once a year.
- Data that is no longer needed is deleted according to the retention schedule, and the deletion is recorded.

## Responsibilities

Data owners decide on classification, access and retention. Everyone who handles data follows the classification rules and reports errors in the data they find.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Quality Assurance department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v3.2 of the Department Operational Guidelines, effective from 2022-02-06 and maintained by the Quality Assurance department.

## Purpose

These guidelines describe the day-to-day working arrangements of the Quality Assurance department, so that responsibilities, working hours and escalation routes are clear to everyone.

## Scope

They apply to all members of the Quality Assurance department, including contractors who work as part of the team.

## Rules

- Core working hours are 10:00 to 16:00 on working days; outside those hours people arrange their time with their manager.
- The team meets weekly to review priorities, progress and blockers, and decisions are noted and shared afterwards.
- Requests to the department are made through its ticket queue or shared mailbox, so that nothing depends on one person's inbox.
- Planned absence is entered in the team calendar in advance, and a colleague is named to cover urgent matters.
- Issues that cannot be resolved within the team within two working days are escalated to the department head.

## Responsibilities

The department head sets priorities and resolves escalations. Team members keep their work visible and raise problems early.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Quality Assurance department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.7 of the Information Security Policy, effective from 2026-03-07 and maintained by the Quality Assurance department.

## Purpose

This policy protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the information that the Quality Assurance department works with.

## Scope

It applies to everyone in the Quality Assurance department and to all devices, systems and information they use for work.

## Rules

- Information is handled according to its classification, and confidential information is not discussed or displayed where others can see or hear it.
- Company devices are encrypted, locked when unattended and kept up to date with security patches.
- Only approved software and cloud services are used for company information.
- Be alert to phishing: do not open unexpected attachments or links, and report suspicious messages to the security team.
- Every security incident or near miss is reported at once, even if it seems minor.

## Responsibilities

Everyone completes the annual security awareness training. Managers make sure the rules are followed in their teams. The security team monitors, advises and responds to incidents.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Quality Assurance department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v2.8 of the Business Process Guidelines, effective from 2025-12-30 and maintained by the Quality Assurance department.

## Purpose

These guidelines describe how the Quality Assurance department documents, runs and improves its regular business processes, so that work is done the same reliable way whoever does it.

## Scope

They apply to all recurring processes owned by the Quality Assurance department and to everyone who takes part in them.

## Rules

- Every recurring process has a named owner and a written description of its steps, inputs, outputs and expected turnaround time.
- Requests enter a process through the agreed channel, so that they can be tracked from start to finish.
- Hand-overs between people or teams are recorded, including what is still open and who is now responsible.
- Problems and delays are raised with the process owner as soon as they are noticed, not at the deadline.
- Each process is reviewed at least once a year and after any serious failure, and the description is updated to match how the work is really done.

## Responsibilities

Process owners keep the descriptions current and measure how the process performs. Team members follow the documented steps and suggest improvements.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Quality Assurance department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

## Purpose

This policy explains the types of leave employees are entitled to and how leave is requested and approved.

It applies to all permanent employees. Interns and contractors follow the leave terms in their own agreements.

Employees plan leave early and hand over their work. Managers approve fairly and make sure the team stays covered. Human Resources keeps the leave records.

This is version v1.0 of the Recruitment Guidelines, effective from 2021-11-06 and maintained by the Human Resources department.

## Purpose

These guidelines make sure that hiring is fair, consistent and based on the needs of the role.

## Scope

They apply to the recruitment of all permanent employees, interns and fixed-term staff.

## Rules

- A vacancy is opened only after the hiring manager and Human Resources have agreed the job description and the budget.
- Vacancies are advertised internally and externally for at least five working days.
- Candidates are assessed against the same written criteria by an interview panel of at least two people.
- Hiring decisions are based on skills and experience. Discrimination on any personal characteristic is prohibited.
- Offers are made in writing by Human Resources after reference and background checks are complete.

## Responsibilities

Hiring managers lead the selection. Human Resources runs the process, keeps the records and gives every interviewed candidate an answer.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Human Resources department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

## Purpose

This policy describes the standard of behaviour the company expects from everyone who works for it.

It applies to all employees, interns and contractors, in the office, when working remotely, at client sites and at company events.

This is version v3.0 of the Financial Audit Policy, effective from 2025-04-15 and maintained by the Finance department.

## Purpose

This policy sets out how the company's financial records are checked, internally and by external auditors, so that they can be trusted.

Finance keeps records ready for audit. Department heads give auditors the information they ask for and correct the findings assigned to them.

This is version v1.5 of the Expense Management Policy, effective from 2023-01-25 and maintained by the Finance department.

## Purpose

This policy explains which business expenses the company pays for and how employees claim them.

## Scope

It applies to all employees who spend money on behalf of the company, including travel, accommodation, meals, training and small purchases.

## Rules

- Expenses must be necessary for work, reasonable in cost and approved by the employee's manager; travel is approved before it is booked.
- Claims are submitted within thirty days of the expense, each with an itemised receipt.
- Travel is booked in economy class and at standard business hotels unless the department head approves an exception in writing.
- Personal expenses, fines and penalties are not reimbursed.
- Approved claims are paid with the next monthly payroll run.

## Responsibilities

Employees claim honestly and keep receipts. Managers check that claims are justified. Finance audits a sample of claims every month.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the Finance department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

It applies to all operating and project budgets in every department.

- Budgets are approved first by the department head, then by the Chief Financial Officer; budgets above the board threshold also need approval from the Chief Executive Officer.
- Spending may not start on an activity that has no approved budget.
- A change of more than ten percent to an approved budget line needs a written revision approved by the same people who approved the original.
- Finance compares actual spending with the budget every month and reports significant differences to the department head.

## Responsibilities

Department heads own their budgets. Finance maintains the approved figures, the revision history and the monthly comparison.

This is version v2.3 of the Data Management Policy, effective from 2023-03-16 and maintained by the Legal department.

## Purpose

This policy sets out how the Legal department classifies, stores, shares and retires the data it creates and uses.

- Data that is no longer needed is deleted according to the retention schedule, and the deletion is recorded.

This is version v2.6 of the Access Control Policy, effective from 2025-04-30 and maintained by the IT Support department.

## Purpose

This policy makes sure that people and systems can reach only the information and tools they need for their work, and nothing more.

## Scope

It covers all company applications, databases, cloud accounts, networks and physical offices, for employees, contractors and service accounts.

## Rules

- Access is granted by job role on the principle of least privilege and must be approved by the employee's manager and the system owner.
- Every person uses their own named account. Shared and generic accounts are not allowed.
- Multi-factor authentication is required for remote access, administrator access and all systems that hold confidential data.
- Managers review the access of their team every quarter and remove anything that is no longer needed.
- Access is removed on the last working day of anyone who leaves, and adjusted within three working days when someone changes role.

## Responsibilities

System owners approve and review access. IT Support carries out the changes and keeps the records. Managers report role changes and departures promptly.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the IT Support department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v2.1 of the Infrastructure Security Policy, effective from 2022-06-27 and maintained by the IT Support department.

## Purpose

This policy sets the security requirements for the servers, networks and cloud services that run the company's systems.

## Scope

It applies to all production and non-production infrastructure, whether hosted in the company's own data centres or in the cloud.

- Infrastructure is built from approved, hardened templates and managed as code, so that every change is reviewed and traceable.

- Administrator access uses individual accounts with multi-factor authentication, and all administrator actions are logged.
- Logs from all systems are collected centrally, kept for at least one year and monitored for signs of attack.

## Responsibilities

The infrastructure team builds and maintains systems to these requirements. The security team runs regular vulnerability scans and an annual penetration test.

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the IT Support department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.1 of the Password Management Policy, effective from 2024-11-16 and maintained by the IT Support department.

## Purpose

This policy sets the rules for creating, using and protecting passwords and other login credentials.

## Scope

It applies to every account used for company work, including service accounts and accounts on third-party services.

## Rules

- Passwords are at least 12 characters long and are not reused between systems.
- Passwords are stored only in the company's approved password manager, never in documents, chats or on paper.
- Passwords are never shared, and no one from the company will ever ask an employee for a password.
- A password is changed immediately if it may have been disclosed. Passwords for administrator accounts are changed at least every 90 days.
- Multi-factor authentication is switched on wherever a system supports it.

## Responsibilities

Every account holder is responsible for their own credentials. IT Support enforces the technical rules and helps with the password manager.

## Exceptions and review

Exceptions need written approval from the head of the IT Support department. This document is reviewed at least once a year, and the version number changes whenever the content does.

This is version v1.1 of the Data Management Policy, effective from 2021-08-25 and maintained by the Executive Office department.

## Purpose

This policy sets out how the Executive Office department classifies, stores, shares and retires the data it creates and uses.

## Scope

It applies to all data owned or processed by the Executive Office department, whether in databases, documents, spreadsheets or reports.

## Rules

- Every data set has an owner and a classification: public, internal, confidential or restricted.
- Data is stored in the approved systems for its classification, never only on a personal device.
- Confidential and restricted data is shared on a need-to-know basis and with the owner's approval.
- Important data is backed up, and the backups are tested by restoring them at least once a year.
- Data that is no longer needed is deleted according to the retention schedule, and the deletion is recorded.

## Responsibilities

Data owners decide on classification, access and retention. Everyone who handles data follows the classification rules and reports errors in the data they find.
